title: LESSON 1 - BEGINNER BHANGRA SERIES | Fundamentals & Bhangra Footwork | BFUNK Dance Tutorials

method.teacher_system: The teacher introduces the curriculum, demonstrates the overall footwork, breaks down three fundamental Bhangra steps (Bedi, Dhamaal, and Punjab) with counts and form tips, and practices them at increasing tempos.

practices.what: Count 4-count slow taps to get used to the weight shift.
Practice the Bedi footwork at a faster tempo.
Practice the Dhamaal footwork step-by-step for 4 counts.
Practice Dhamaal at an increased tempo.

adaptations.difficulty: Natural inclination to raise knees higher or add variations
adaptations.adjustment: Raise the knee higher or bring the foot back for different stylistic variations.

adaptations.difficulty: Limited flexibility making it hard to lift the leg high
adaptations.adjustment: Lift the leg and keep it right past the knee as a starting goal.

beliefs.belief: Anyone starting fresh, staying active, or returning after years away is in the right place.

moments.says: The teacher welcomes the learner to the beginner Bhangra series and validates starting from scratch.
The teacher points out the common error of slamming the whole foot down and demonstrates the proper technique using the balls of the feet.
The teacher introduces variations and reassures the learner that raising knees higher or adding styling is optional.
The teacher offers a modification for flexibility and encourages starting at an attainable level.
The teacher praises the learner for completing the count and explains the purpose behind light foot placement.

mentor.what_stays: The teacher leaves the learner feeling capable, energized, and welcomed as a dancer ready to tackle foundational Bhangra steps.

struggles.theme: Feeling uncoordinated like a drunken giraffe
Not coordinated enough to do the steps

clicked.theme: Breaking down steps simply made it possible for someone with two left feet

meant.theme: Feels great to dance again after a long time

method.limits: The video ends before completing the instruction of the third step (Punjab).
